supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 recorded a network logon for omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01. At 13:41:49 UTC, PowerShell ran under omar.haddad's matching logon ID with the command to execute \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1, consistent with the organization’s described workstation-patching practice.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows 11 KB .msu quietly, and the proxy recorded a Windows Update Agent connection transferring about 38.8 MB. These events are consistent with patch deployment, though they do not establish successful installation.
The PowerShell process ended at 13:42:39 UTC, about 50 seconds after it started, consistent with the reported brief appearance.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection status reports a winsec and Sysmon outage on WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC. This is not the alerted host, WS-MLOPEZ-01.
The process and command-line evidence does not establish whether a console was visible to Maria or whether she interacted with it.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish whether Deploy-Patches.ps1's contents were the approved version or whether the patch installation completed successfully.
The records do not establish whether omar.haddad's credentials or the admin workstation were compromised.
unrelated_findings: The proxy recorded a GoogleDriveFS connection to clients4.google.com and a DropboxUpdate connection to desktop.dropbox.com. These appear to involve unapproved cloud-storage services under the supplied software policy and should be reviewed in a separate ticket; they do not determine the disposition of the PowerShell alert. (T014-00219, T014-00286)
